question: Should Crabbox support durable, revocable read-only device credentials as a first-party coordinator API, rather than limiting companion status access to existing portal sessions?
rationale: This decision controls a new public authentication principal, its lifetime and revocation guarantees, the portal browser authority boundary, and the operational ownership expected after release; code tests cannot choose that product contract.

options.title: Sponsor read-only device pairing
options.body: Accept the documented device principal as a supported coordinator API and assign ongoing ownership for the credential lifecycle, revocation semantics, and security boundary.

options.title: Pause for companion scope
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/778 selects the supported first-party device and authentication direction.

options.title: Keep status inside portal sessions
options.body: Prefer the existing portal-authenticated path and defer durable device credentials until a broader client contract is approved.

recommendation.title: Pause for companion scope
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but do not merge until https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/778 selects the supported first-party device and authentication direction.

likelyOwner.reason: The related open design issue is the clearest available place where the outstanding mobile scope and credential-boundary decision is framed.
